title: Potential-energy changes, reference zero and elastic storage

units.content:
## 7. Energy

Energy is defined as the capacity of a body to perform work. It is a scalar quantity sharing the same SI unit as work (**Joule**).

### 7.1 Potential Energy

#### 7.1.1 Concept
Potential energy ($U$) is the energy possessed by a body or system by virtue of its position, configuration, or spatial state. It is independent of the dynamic trajectory by which the system arrived at that state.

Potential energy is intrinsically a relative quantity and requires the choice of a reference zero level ($U = 0$).

#### 7.1.2 Definition
$$\Delta U = U_B - U_A = -W_{c}(A \to B) = -\int_{A}^{B} \vec{F}_c \cdot d\vec{r}$$

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Potential energy is defined **strictly for conservative forces**. It cannot be defined for non-conservative forces because their work depends on the path taken.

#### 7.1.3 Gravitational Potential Energy (GPE)
When lifting a body of mass $m$ vertically through height $h$:
$$W_{\text{ext}} = mgh, \quad W_{\text{gravity}} = -mgh$$
$$\Delta U = -W_{\text{gravity}} = mgh$$

- When the center of mass of a body is raised by height $h$, $\Delta \text{GPE} = +mgh$.
- When the center of mass of a body is lowered by distance $h$, $\Delta \text{GPE} = -mgh$.

#### 7.1.4 Elastic Potential Energy
Work performed against the internal restoring force of an elastic medium is stored as elastic potential energy.

#### 7.1.5 Nature of Restoring Force
When a spring is stretched or compressed by displacement $x$ from its natural length, it exerts a Hookean restoring force:
$$F_s = -kx$$

The work done by the spring force during displacement from $0$ to $x$ is:
$$W_s = \int_{0}^{x} (-kx')dx' = -\frac{1}{2}kx^2$$

The elastic potential energy stored in the spring is:
$$U = -W_s = \frac{1}{2}kx^2$$
| WPE-N06 | §7.1 PE: GPE, elastic PE | WEP-05 Gravitational and elastic PE | core | 5 |

content.title: Gravitational & Elastic Potential Energy Wells
content.definition: Potential energy U represents stored energy of configuration defined exclusively for conservative interactions via Delta U = -W_c.
canonical_rules: Gravitational potential energy near Earth surface: U_g = m g h (relative to chosen datum h = 0).
Ideal spring elastic potential energy: U_s = 0.5 k x^2 (where x is extension/compression from unstretched equilibrium).
Datum choice is an arbitrary gauge convention; only potential energy differences Delta U have physical significance.
operational_heuristics: Declare datum line U = 0 at the lowest geometric point or relaxed spring position.
Account for both gravitational and elastic components in total potential energy: U = U_g + U_s.
boundary_conditions: x = 0: U_s = 0 (relaxed spring stores zero energy).

content.title: Grade 9 work and mechanical-energy equations are one ledger
content.badge_reason: The arithmetic is direct; the difficult part is deciding which account and relation the situation permits.
entry_assumptions: Can classify work sign and decide whether extra frictional/outside transfer closes or opens the mechanical-energy account.
content.inferential_jump: Work, kinetic energy, near-Earth gravitational potential-energy change, work-energy and mechanical-energy conservation are linked bookkeeping statements with explicit body/system, frame/reference and model conditions; K+U conservation is only the zero-nonconservative-transfer special case.

teaching_path.action: Choose the body/system, displacement direction, reference frame and height reference before calculating.
teaching_path.why_valid: Work sign and energy values depend on these declarations.
teaching_path.output: chosen body/account; path direction; frame; height reference.

teaching_path.action: Use W = F_parallel s, K = 0.5 m v^2 and Delta U_g = m g Delta h for the matching quantities.
teaching_path.why_valid: Each gate-owned relation defines one distinct part of the energy ledger.
teaching_path.output: W = F_parallel s; K = 0.5 m v^2; Delta U_g = m g Delta h, all in joules under their stated conditions.

teaching_path.action: Relate net work to Delta K, or equate endpoint K + U only when no extra transfer crosses the chosen account.
teaching_path.why_valid: The work-energy theorem and mechanical-energy conservation answer different bookkeeping questions.
teaching_path.output: W_net = Delta K; closed account -> K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f.

teaching_path.action: Use a rough-track counterexample to test whether a claimed K + U conservation statement is allowed.
teaching_path.why_valid: Frictional transfer opens the mechanical account and invalidates unchanged K + U by itself.
teaching_path.output: rough path -> include transfer; do not force K + U constant.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Once kinetic and potential energy appear, K + U must always be conserved.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A block descends the same height on a rough track and a smooth track. Must the final kinetic energies match?
misconceptions.repair: Inventory transfers first. Friction can move energy out of the mechanical account, so identical endpoints do not guarantee the same K + U ledger.

exit_task.prompt: A 2 kg object moves at 3 m/s. Find its translational kinetic energy. Then state what additional condition is required before using K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f for a later motion.

answer.summary: K = 9 J. Mechanical-energy conservation additionally requires that no frictional or outside transfer change the chosen K + U account.
reasoning: The conservation equation is conditional, not automatic.
If friction or an outside agent transfers energy, that transfer must be included.
answer.check: Doubling the speed to 6 m/s would quadruple K to 36 J.

content.research_contribution: Local quantitative Grade-9 Work/Energy closure enriched from prior internal engineering with system-boundary, reference-consistency and model-validity checks.

predict.prompt: Two 2 kg objects move at 3 m/s and 6 m/s. Does the faster one have twice the kinetic energy?
predict.defensible_answer: No. K depends on speed squared, so doubling speed gives four times the kinetic energy.

attempt.produces: A kinetic-energy calculation plus a conservation-condition statement.

rubric.criterion: Computes kinetic energy with speed squared.
States the no-extra-transfer condition before using mechanical-energy conservation.
rubric.evidence_of: Treating conservation as a conditional ledger.

accepted: 2 kg at 3 m/s -> 9 J; conserve K+U only when no extra transfer changes the account.
rejected: K = m v or automatic K+U conservation on a rough path.

route.ask: Which energy depends on motion in the declared frame?
How does speed enter that relation?
What transfer inventory must be checked before conserving K + U?
What does a rough path do to the account?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: The teaching path builds the ledger from declarations; the learner route starts from a kinetic-energy scaling question and then tests the conservation boundary.

boundary_test.prompt: If a body is instantaneously at rest in the declared frame, what is its translational kinetic energy?
boundary_test.confirms: K is nonnegative and vanishes at zero speed.

content.expression: Delta U_g = m g Delta h
content.meaning: Near Earth's surface with approximately uniform g, gravitational potential-energy change equals mass times g times vertical height change.
conditions: g is approximately uniform over the height change.
One height reference and positive-up convention are used.

derivation.action: Multiply mass, local g and signed vertical height change.
derivation.why_valid: REL-GRAVITATIONAL-POTENTIAL-NEAR-EARTH owns the near-Earth change relation.
derivation.output: Delta U_g = m g Delta h.

limits: Only changes are physically meaningful until a zero reference is declared.
Do not extend uniform g to large height ranges without review.
checks: Raising the body gives positive Delta U_g under positive-up convention.
Returning to the original height gives net Delta U_g = 0.

oracle.description: How this exit answer is stood behind. Exactly one of: `verification`, naming a subject validator and binding its inputs to declared data; `held_by`, naming the known issue that explains why no oracle exists yet; or `no_numeric_claim`, saying why the answer asserts no computed value. Silence is not an option, because the exit answer is what a learner measures themselves against.

elicitation.description: The self-tutor cycle. Four of its six steps live here; diagnose and repair are misconceptions[].wrong_idea, .diagnostic_prompt and .repair, which already hold the same claim for the declarative product. predict.description: Pose the decision before revealing anything.

prompt.description: The decision, posed so a learner can commit to an answer.

defensible_answer.description: The answer that commitment is judged against. A prompt with no defensible answer is a musing, not a prediction.

attempt.description: What the learner produces, and how it closes without a tutor.

produces.description: What the learner should construct, draw, discriminate or explain.

closure.description: Which form of closure this attempt uses. Each value demands something the others do not, so that none is a synonym an author can pick to avoid work: MODEL_RESPONSE requires model_response, CRITERIA requires rubric, and RUBRIC requires rubric with accepted and rejected examples -- the spec's 'a rubric plus representative accepted and rejected answers', which is the stronger claim of the three.

model_response.description: Closure as one response, where one is right.

rubric.description: Closure as a rubric, where several responses are valid.

rejected.description: Representative responses it rejects. A rubric with no rejected example has not been tested against anything.

task.description: Schema 0.2.0: the concrete reconstruction task the learner performs (a body, givens, numbers or a situation). `produces` says what the attempt should contain; `task` is what the learner is asked to do. Rendered as the Core1B attempt.

representation_ref.description: The representation of this task's own situation (its bodies and values), shown with the Core1B attempt. When absent, Core1B falls back to the first construction unit's (Core1A) figure, which depicts a different situation.

stage_refs.description: Stages of representation_ref safe to show before the attempt; default is the first stage only.

reconstruct.description: The correct construction reached the way a learner would reach it. Held as questions rather than statements: teaching_path is the expert's summary, and a reconstruct route made of statements is that summary under a different key, which is exactly how this product became the declarative one.

route.description: The sequence of asks. Order is meaning: each one is answerable only once the previous has been answered.

ask.description: A question that moves the learner one decision forward. A sentence with a question mark on it is not an ask; the learner must be able to get it wrong.

why_this_ask.description: Why this question rather than another at this point. An author who cannot say this has ordered the route by the expert's convenience.

from_step_ref.description: The teaching_path step this ask arrives at, where one exists. Absent means the learner's route genuinely departs from the expert's, which is why both are held.

differs_from_teaching_path.description: How the learner's route differs from the expert's construction. This is the sentence a reviewer checks the A/B claim against, so it may not restate the teaching path it claims to differ from.

prompt.description: A limiting case, reversal or edge condition.

confirms.description: What passing it establishes, stated so that a recall question cannot be passed off as a boundary test.

answer.description: What passing it looks like. The shared closure invariant has no exception for the last prompt in a cycle.

compact_anchor.description: Schema 0.2.0: the Core1 compact anchor, a one-line instance of the governing relation that makes the map usable before Core1A.

representation_ref.description: The representation of this compact anchor's own situation, shown on the Core1 map. When absent, Core1 falls back to the microtopic's first representation_refs entry, which is often shared across microtopics.

role.description: What the step does to the state. A DECLARE step fixes a convention or a domain and legitimately produces no computation; a TRANSFORM step changes the mathematical state and must show the changed state, not describe it; a VERIFY step checks a result against something already established.

source_ref.description: The source this step's claim rests on. Absent means the step is the author's own construction, which is legitimate and is not the same as source-supported.

content.description: One distinct decision/event of a microtopic's construction, taught as its own unit (Core1A) and reconstructed in Core1B.

extensions.description: Namespaced unit-level extensions. Repeated blueprint applicability may use extensions['grade9v3:component_waivers'] with the same {COMPONENT_ID: reason} contract as a top-level record.

decision.description: The move the learner must make in this unit, in words.

reveal_stage_refs.description: That representation's reveal stages used by this unit, in order.

worked_anchor_ref.description: Question (exposure CORE1A) whose route exercises this unit's move.

bank_anchor_ref.description: A question of the product's bank (an owner-supplied or exam question, not a question of this package) that this unit works through as its worked example: the page shows the question as its owner wrote it with its verified route. Resolved when the product is built, so a package does not carry a copy of the question. Use it for the question the unit builds toward; use worked_anchor_ref for a question the package authors itself.

crux_question_refs.description: Bank questions whose crux this unit builds: the move a learner is most likely to miss in each. The toughest question of a set must be named here by a unit of the concept it belongs to; its difficulty band does not prescribe the unit's component or panel count.

crux_step_ref.description: The teaching_path step of this unit (one of its step_refs) that builds the move named questions in crux_question_refs turn on. The page marks that step, so a reader can see where the unit does the work the hard question needs.

misconception_indexes.description: Indexes into microtopic.misconceptions (wrong path, diagnose, repair).

relation_refs.description: The microtopic's relations this unit uses, shown as the unit's own equation card. Absent: the first unit shows all of the microtopic's relations.

migrated_from.description: Set by package_migrate.py when the unit was derived mechanically (e.g. 'teaching_path'); cleared when an author reviews it.

decision_from.description: Set instead of `decision` when the unit's decision is the microtopic's own field (migration); one source of truth, no copied text.

extensions.description: Namespaced subject extensions; no scientific authority is inferred.

scene_instances.description: Concrete figures satisfying this representation. Everything above states what a figure of this kind must show; an instance states one actual figure, bound to the data it draws, so the library can compile a figure instead of only requiring one.

element.description: The part of the picture, named as required_elements names it.

symbol.description: The symbol it stands for, as the governing relation writes it.

in_words.description: The same thing said in words, which is the third leg of the bridge.

correspondence.description: The representation bridge. required_elements says what the picture must contain and the relation's symbols say what the algebra means, but nothing bound one to the other, so the correspondence a learner must make was asserted rather than held. Naming all three legs is what makes it explicit in both directions rather than a caption pointing one way.

interactive_resource_refs.description: ACTIVITY resources that implement or manipulate this canonical representation. The representation remains academic authority.

gate_relation_ref.description: The engineering gate relation this is a bound copy of. Subject truth is owned by the gate registry; the library holds a copy so the compiler can reach it, and that copy is checked against the owner. null says no gate backs this relation: that is true of a subject that declares no gates (a sandbox, or a contract-only subject), and for a subject that has gates Shared/library/authority.py reports it as GATE_RELATION_BINDING_ABSENT.
